title: Wintering
haiku:
Pipes I used to teach
now the target of a war
may God keep them warm
headline: Russia is preparing its most powerful strike yet on Ukraine's energy grid to freeze the country through winter.

title: Leakproof
haiku:
He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true
headline: An elderly man was reunited with the children he saved from Nazi occupation decades ago, in a moment arranged by Esther Rantzen.

title: Outflow
haiku:
Twenty-three years drain
the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain
headline: After 23 years, the last American forces have withdrawn from Iraq, leaving the country's future uncertain.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Storm drains gasp, then flood
I sized these pipes for less rain
the sky forgot code
headline: A powerful nor'easter caused flooding across the northeastern US, prompting New York and New Jersey to declare states of emergency.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Newsrooms shut the valve,
one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.
headline: Major U.S. news outlets boycotted a shared White House video feed of Trump in protest at new restrictions on the press pool.

title: Pooled
haiku:
I've seen valves shut tight
the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight
headline: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are suing the Trump administration after being denied White House press access.

title: Discovery
haiku:
Old pipes hold no lies
a judge opens the sluice gate
truth finally flows
headline: A federal judge ordered Fox News to turn over hundreds of documents in a shareholder lawsuit over its election-fraud coverage.

title: Unclaimed
haiku:
No flag on the ice
just old friends drafting a deal
the map holds its line
headline: The US and Denmark reached a deal over Greenland, defusing Trump's earlier annexation threats.

title: Relief
haiku:
One valve turned by hand
Seoul says no more troops abroad
pressure finds its ease
headline: South Korea's president rejected Trump's request to send troops against Iran, choosing restraint over escalation.

title: Overtime
haiku:
More days in the pipe
a valve cracked, and time flows on
I'll take the extra.
headline: A new drug is extending the lives of some breast cancer patients.

title: Tributary
haiku:
Old allies reroute
round a wall no one can name
water finds its way
headline: The EU offered to make Canada an 'associate member' as both countries' ties to the U.S. grow strained.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its seat
the court refused the backflow
votes still reach the main
headline: The Supreme Court blocked Trump's plan to restrict mail-in ballots ahead of the midterms.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its line
someone tried to brew plague code
and the pipe held fast
headline: Anthropic disclosed that it detected and blocked a likely attempt to use its AI models to help develop biological weapons.

title: Spigot
haiku:
Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks
headline: Trump promised $5,000 payments to Americans if Republicans win the midterm elections.

title: Crudeness
haiku:
Oil pressure red-lines
old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this
headline: Iran signaled readiness to escalate conflict with the U.S. as oil surged past $100 a barrel amid intensifying Middle East turmoil.

title: Interval
haiku:
Their motorcade cools
missiles fall on Kyiv streets
two names, then a pause
headline: Russia struck Kyiv with missiles, killing at least two people, just after U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner departed from peace talks.

title: Shortfall
haiku:
Far right rises, short
one seat from the flood gate's edge
still the old seal holds
headline: Germany's far-right AfD won Saxony-Anhalt's state election but fell just short of the majority needed to govern alone.

title: Loaner
haiku:
A borrowed kidney
keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows
headline: A genetically modified pig kidney has kept working inside a U.S. man's body for a record 271 days.

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Calm month, then backflow
the oil climbs where pressure breaks
old valves still can hold
headline: The United States and Iran exchanged military strikes overnight, ending a month-long calm and sending global oil prices toward $90 a barrel as world finance officials meet.

title: Waterline
haiku:
Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise
headline: Nepal's flash floods swept away a town, rescuers pulled survivors from a hydropower tunnel, and officials warned a glacial lake could breach and flood again.

title: Flushed
haiku:
Neighbors trade barbs north
the throne room short on tissue
even pipes need friends
headline: The US and Canada's trade war escalates with tariffs up to 50%, driving a surge in American toilet paper prices.

title: Unsanctioned
haiku:
Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water
headline: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.

title: Repressure
haiku:
Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow
headline: Analysts say Democrats' chances of winning back the Senate are improving.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge cracks the valve
seventy-five nations' door
swings open again
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration's visa ban on 75 countries was illegal.

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear
headline: Spain reversed a policy that trapped migrant children in Ceuta, clearing the way for roughly 500 to move to the mainland.

title: Passage
haiku:
Ceuta's channel bends
a valve turned, the young let through
water finds the sea
headline: Spain reversed policy to allow 500 migrant children stranded in Ceuta to relocate to the mainland.

title: Retrofit
haiku:
My own blood, retooled,
learns to filter what returns—
old pipes, new gasket.
headline: A new personalized cancer vaccine trial showed it can prevent the disease from returning.

title: Eclipsical
haiku:
Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer
headline: A total solar eclipse swept across the UK, Europe, and Spain, drawing millions of onlookers outside to watch together.

title: Foundation
haiku:
The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now
headline: A major earthquake struck western Colombia, killing more than 130 people and leveling homes.

title: Setback
haiku:
Another blueprint
shelved before the concrete dries—
still, I mix more sand
headline: Israel rejected President Trump's 15-point plan to disarm Hamas in Gaza.

title: Backflow
haiku:
One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows
headline: The Senate let Trump's push for a new voting bill quietly die rather than pass it.

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted
headline: The Women's Professional Baseball League made its historic debut.

title: Spillover
haiku:
Old pipes want one crack
to spread beyond one border
I have watched this flood
headline: U.S. and Saudi airstrikes on Iran-backed militias have widened the conflict, drawing in Jordan and other regional players.

title: Grapeshot
haiku:
Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well
headline: Wildfires are closing in on Madrid and Bordeaux's vineyards as firefighters in France and Spain race to contain them before an incoming heat wave.

title: Cordon
haiku:
Twenty years, same town
the fever met its old drain
and stayed underground
headline: A Ugandan town that endured an Ebola outbreak two decades ago has successfully contained a new one this time.

title: Sluice
haiku:
Enough hands, one valve
turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on
headline: India's education minister resigned, handing a win to student protesters who had organized against him.

title: Seepage
haiku:
Signal finds the crack
young hands raise their phones like pipes
truth still finds its grade
headline: Young protesters in India used smartphones to route around Modi government media controls and organize demonstrations.

title: Satirical
haiku:
a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat
headline: In India, a protest that began as satire grows into a nationwide challenge to Narendra Modi's government.

title: Removable
haiku:
no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote
headline: Andy Burnham replaces Keir Starmer as the United Kingdom's prime minister

title: Pitched
haiku:
a billion of us
packed around one patch of grass —
the good kind of war
headline: Spain and Argentina meet in the FIFA World Cup final at New York New Jersey Stadium

title: Asymmetrical
headline: Fighting intensifies with strikes on critical infrastructure as US-Iran war widens

title: Structural
haiku:
I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break
headline: Iran and US widen attacks as renewed conflict shows no sign of de-escalating

title: Sweepingly
haiku:
the sweepers come out
as they did in every war —
brooms outlast bombers
headline: Kyiv hit again as Ukraine reports two dead in Russian strike

title: Half-Mast
haiku:
I outlive them all —
men I argued with for years
the flag still half-mast
headline: Lindsey Graham, longtime South Carolina senator, dies at 71

title: Inheritance
haiku:
sons avenging sons —
the oldest sewage on earth
still flows down to us
headline: Iran's Supreme Leader pledges revenge for slain father and predecessor

title: Photogenic
haiku:
the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens
headline: US, Iran threaten more attacks as strikes continue, Trump attends NATO summit

title: Handover
haiku:
hand over the keys —
any government that lets
children out at dusk
headline: Hamas dissolves Gaza government, ceding civilian rule to technocratic committee

title: Remembrance
haiku:
each name read aloud —
no nation is too broken
to remember well
headline: Venezuela quake death toll rises to 3,342 as families search for the missing

title: Anniversary
haiku:
two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says
even when we don't
headline: Nation celebrates 250th anniversary of American independence

title: Meteorology
haiku:
"progress," someone says —
a word I trust like weather
still, I check the sky
headline: US-Iran talks in Doha make 'positive progress,' Qatar says

title: Reversible
haiku:
we warmed the whole sea —
my grandchildren swim in it —
we can cool it too
headline: Global oceans break June temperature record amid fears of 'uncharted territory'

title: Birthright
haiku:
the court holds the line:
born here is born here. full stop.
some days we're still us
headline: Supreme Court upholds birthright citizenship, ruling against Trump's order

title: Underdogs
haiku:
the small island wins —
somewhere the odds-makers weep
good. let them. dance on
headline: Cape Verde becomes smallest nation ever to reach World Cup knockout stage

title: Barehanded
haiku:
the ground breaks its word —
neighbors, not governments, dig
first, and bare-handed
headline: Twin earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 strike northwestern Venezuela

title: Viticulture
haiku:
forty-four degrees —
the old vines have seen empires
never such a sun
headline: France records hottest day ever at 44.3C amid European heatwave

title: Hydrology
haiku:
one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat
headline: US and Iran open ceasefire talks in Switzerland as Hormuz stays closed

title: Endurance
haiku:
thirty-two names read —
the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling
headline: Israeli airstrikes kill at least 32 in southern Lebanon

title: Briefly
haiku:
another ceasefire —
I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely
headline: US announces Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire after deadly strikes on Lebanon

title: Reparable
haiku:
the strait opens wide —
gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things
headline: Iran and US sign accord; Strait of Hormuz to reopen as blockades end

title: Encore
haiku:
in a locked-down year,
we still reached the rusted plains,
hope wearing a mask
headline: NASA's Perseverance rover lands on Mars

title: Threshold
haiku:
a sleeve rolled at dawn,
the whole locked world leaned in close—
one small needle's prick
headline: The first person receives a COVID-19 vaccine outside of trials

title: Portrait
haiku:
we drew the abyss—
a ring of fire round the dark—
the void has a face
headline: Astronomers reveal the first image ever taken of a black hole

title: Ripple
haiku:
two black holes had died
the ripple crossed a billion
years to chime on earth
headline: Scientists announce the first detection of gravitational waves

title: Comeback
haiku:
nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled
headline: New Horizons makes humanity's first close flyby of Pluto

title: Wedlock
haiku:
the court read the words—
love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on
headline: The U.S. Supreme Court affirms marriage equality nationwide

title: Terminal
haiku:
he stepped off a ledge
twenty four miles of falling—
the sky held its breath
headline: Felix Baumgartner skydives from the edge of space

title: Skycrane
haiku:
seven minutes, dark,
cables lowered a robot,
Mars held its red breath
headline: NASA's Curiosity rover lands safely on Mars

title: Resurface
haiku:
sixty-nine days dark—
one by one the capsule climbs,
Chile holds its breath
headline: All 33 Chilean miners are rescued alive after 69 days underground

title: Manual
haiku:
we spelled out the book
three billion letters counted—
ourselves, in plain text
headline: The Human Genome Project is completed

title: Keel
haiku:
a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends
headline: The first module of the International Space Station reaches orbit

title: Airbag
haiku:
wrapped in airbags, it
bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars
headline: The Pathfinder mission lands on Mars with the Sojourner rover

title: Ewenique
haiku:
one cell learned a trick
and grew into wool and legs—
the flock gained a twin
headline: Dolly the sheep, the first cloned mammal, is born

title: Freeman
haiku:
the long walk was done
he took the oath as free man
a nation stood tall
headline: Nelson Mandela is inaugurated as South Africa's president

title: Handshake
haiku:
two shores, one long grudge—
a train now slides beneath waves,
England meets France now
headline: The Channel Tunnel opens, linking Britain and France

title: Weave
haiku:
one man strung a thread
through each door around the world
and called it open
headline: Tim Berners-Lee makes the World Wide Web public

title: Broadcast
haiku:
two stages, one world,
the whole planet passed a hat,
and we all watched close
headline: Live Aid unites the world in a concert for famine relief

title: Vanished
haiku:
an ancient killer
we hunted it to nothing—
the world scarred, but whole
headline: The World Health Organization declares smallpox eradicated

title: Longshot
haiku:
twenty kids on skates,
stood up to the biggest team,
and time ran out first
headline: The U.S. hockey team upsets the Soviets in the Miracle on Ice

title: Mixtape
haiku:
we pressed our whole world
onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home
headline: Voyager 1 launches, carrying the Golden Record to the stars

title: Kin
haiku:
bones in the dry wash
the radio sang her name
grandmother, hello
headline: Lucy, an ancient human ancestor, is discovered in Ethiopia

title: Speck
haiku:
a grain of desert
learns to hold a thought and count
the future got small
headline: Intel releases the first commercial microprocessor

title: Untethered
haiku:
a piano sighs,
no heaven, no hell, just us,
the world holds its breath
headline: John Lennon's Imagine is released

title: Lo
haiku:
we typed out login
the wire failed at two letters
lo, the world began
headline: The first message is sent over ARPANET, ancestor of the internet

title: Overview
haiku:
we watched in gray light,
a man stepped onto the moon—
the whole earth held still
headline: Apollo 11 lands the first humans on the Moon

title: Overhead
haiku:
cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage
headline: The Beatles play their final rooftop concert

title: Seasoned
haiku:
four lads in mustache—
a marching band full of dreams,
the needle drops now
headline: The Beatles release Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band

title: Ascent
haiku:
heat shimmers the mall—
one voice climbs the marble steps
and will not come down
headline: Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his I Have a Dream speech

title: Splashdown
haiku:
fifteen minutes up,
a splash, a sailor's salute,
and the free world cheered
headline: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space

title: Outbound
haiku:
one man, then the sky,
he circled the blue marble,
and came home smiling
headline: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human to reach space

title: Bottom
haiku:
down past all sunlight,
seven miles of patient dark—
two men touched the floor
headline: The Trieste carries two men to the deepest point of the ocean

title: Alarm
haiku:
a beach-ball of steel
beeped once round the sleeping earth—
and nobody slept
headline: Sputnik launches, opening the Space Age

title: Opening
haiku:
the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open
headline: Disneyland opens its gates

title: Deliverance
haiku:
the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again
headline: The Salk polio vaccine is declared safe and effective

title: Kinship
haiku:
two brothers, one blood,
a kidney passed like a gift—
no war in the flesh
headline: Surgeons perform the first successful kidney transplant

title: Fineprint
haiku:
the world, still bleeding,
wrote down what a person's owed—
ink dried into law
headline: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

title: Switch
haiku:
three men in a lab
coaxed a crystal to say yes—
the glass tube grew old
headline: Bell Labs demonstrates the first transistor

title: Holdout
haiku:
a fossil surfaced
flapping, blue, and very much
alive, unaware
headline: A living coelacanth, thought extinct for ages, is found alive

title: Span
haiku:
fog swallowed the strait—
we strung two towers, rust-red,
and walked clean across
headline: The Golden Gate Bridge opens to the public

title: Skyfloor
haiku:
hard times, hungry streets—
still we raised a spire of steel,
the sky gained a floor
headline: The Empire State Building opens

title: Runt
haiku:
a farm boy blinked twice
between two star-crowded plates—
one small dot had moved
headline: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto

title: Bloom
haiku:
a moldy dish, left
by pure accident, on this—
death lost its footing
headline: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin

title: Wonders
haiku:
a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes
headline: Howard Carter opens the tomb of Tutankhamun

title: Reprieve
haiku:
the wasting child slept,
a needle full of borrowed
time—and she woke thin
headline: Insulin is first used to save a young diabetic patient

title: Ballot
haiku:
one state, then the vote—
the ballot box learned her name,
a signature, cast
headline: The 19th Amendment secures American women the right to vote

title: Curvature
haiku:
the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky
headline: Eclipse observations confirm Einstein's general relativity

title: Radiant
haiku:
she boiled tons of ore
to find a pinch that glowed blue—
night forgot to fall
headline: Marie and Pierre Curie announce the discovery of radium

title: Seethrough
haiku:
a strange light passed through
his wife's hand bloomed into bone—
the ring outlived skin
headline: Wilhelm Roentgen discovers X-rays

title: Sugarplum
haiku:
a toy soldier wakes,
snow falls, sugarplums take flight,
and mice learn to dance
headline: Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premieres

title: Click
haiku:
you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays
headline: George Eastman patents the Kodak roll-film camera

title: Reprieve
haiku:
a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn
headline: Louis Pasteur successfully tests his rabies vaccine

title: Summons
haiku:
come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in
headline: Alexander Graham Bell makes the first telephone call

title: Spike
haiku:
two rails reached for hands
a golden spike rang them shut
the coasts shook hands, done
headline: The transcontinental railroad is completed at Promontory Summit

title: Unshackled
haiku:
December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law
headline: The 13th Amendment abolishes slavery in the United States

title: Freehand
haiku:
the new year turned once—
a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men
headline: The Emancipation Proclamation takes effect

title: Elsewhere
haiku:
they cut, he dreamed on
a vapor closed the mind's door—
no scream, only sleep
headline: The first public demonstration of surgical anesthesia

title: Pencil
haiku:
they aimed a pencil
at one dark spot in the sky—
and found a planet
headline: Neptune is discovered, exactly where mathematics predicted

title: Silence
haiku:
he could not hear it—
joy poured from a silent man,
the hall wept and clapped
headline: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony premieres

title: Vacca
haiku:
a farm boy's cowpox,
one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
we named it vaccine
headline: Edward Jenner performs the first vaccination against smallpox

title: Entourage
haiku:
four small lights in line
swung round Jupiter each night—
the earth lost its throne
headline: Galileo sees Jupiter's moons through his telescope
